quotes.text: Developing a strategy for artificial intelligence will help put our country on stronger footing as we recover from the coronavirus pandemic and rebuild towards a better future. We must continue to prioritize research and development in order to stay ahead of our adversaries who are actively developing AI capabilities with nefarious intent,

Congress must ensure that the United States leads the world in AI. Innovative projects in AI have the potential to support our infrastructure and our economy and maximize human capability and ingenuity. But there are also serious concerns about the dangerous potential of AI in the hands of corrupt powers with nefarious objectives as well as unintended consequences from well-meaning programmers. Developing a strategy for AI that prepares our country’s workforce and shapes ethical guidelines around ethical values will help put our country on a stronger footing.

Congress must continue to prioritize research and development in order to stay ahead of our adversaries who are actively developing AI capabilities with nefarious intent. I look forward to working with the Task Force to lay out concrete steps for achieving that, considering both the benefits of deploying AI in our society, and the guardrails necessary to ensure it remains trustworthy and safe.

One of the important things, in this context, is that you and the President inherited a paradigm where China was outpacing us for world dominance for the next century. The President has turned the corner on that. Now, the keys to that, we can look at AI or other economic impacts, but those really come down to energy production… Connected to that is the importance of speed in getting that done,

I’ve yet to meet a person at any meeting who’s willing to give up their cell phone or computer. We are certainly in an AI race against China. Now, having said that, there’s a wrong way to do data centers and a right way to do data centers.

It’s important that local leaders are making sure that it’s done the right way. From a federal perspective, the President has put out an executive order. We’re encouraging them to bring their own water and bring their own power. [...] You don’t want a data center be competing against the local communities for those resources. So a lot of it comes down to how it’s done and making sure that it’s done right.
